A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LeanAgent and contain readable main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.7. Content can be matched reliably despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v7 reports original theorem-proving experiments across 23 repositories, lifelong-learning ablations, and MiniF2F test results, including LeanAgent proving 93/244 test theorems.

after.justification: v8 retains those original experiments and additionally reports results for the ReProver+ fine-tuning baseline in Table 2.

M1.justification: The complexity-based curriculum, dynamic database, one-epoch progressive retriever training, and best-first proof search remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 discusses possible adaptations to other LLMs without implementing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 23 repositories, initial and subsequent curricula, MiniF2F scenarios, and alternate-PFR evaluation. Removing the alternate-PFR row from Table 2 does not remove that scenario: its analysis remains in Appendix A.5.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds ReProver+, described as ReProver updated on all 23 repositories at once. The static ReProver comparison and seven existing ablation variants remain. Newly discussed Llemma and DeepSeek-Prover models are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Tables 2 and 10 switch from proof counts to per-repository accuracy, and Section 4.3 removes the composite score while retaining six metrics. ReProver+ adds a pooled-training control. Appendix A.2 changes the stated EWC selection criterion from composite score to stability/plasticity scores, retaining lambda = 0.1; this does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds the ReProver+ control to examine curriculum learning against pooled fine-tuning. Existing EWC, repository-order, and dataset-merging ablations, alternate-PFR exploit analysis, and appendix proof case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Both retain the same 3% threshold for calling improvements significant; the CFR discussion's ±0.01 describes differences between setups.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds nine ReProver+ results: LeanAgent exceeds it on four listed repositories and ties on five. Table 4 removes composite-score results, including LeanAgent's 0.94. The separate alternate-PFR breakdown is dropped, although its successes remain discussed. Retained proof counts convert consistently to percentages, and all six remaining lifelong-learning metric rows and MiniF2F test results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 removes the proposed composite score's mathematical definition as a weighted combination of normalized metrics. The theorem-complexity definition, EWC objective, tentative TPPS formulation in Appendix A.7, and displayed Lean proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the description of 155 theorems from previously unproved formally by humans to having missing formal proofs in the repositories. v8 also withdraws the near-perfect 94% composite-score headline. The central lifelong-learning framework and generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 adds architectural qualifications for adapting LeanAgent to non-retrieval LLMs and explains the unused alternative search strategy. Appendix A.5 qualifies the ReProver+ comparison as non-direct and adds arguments about retraining costs, data scarcity, and backward transfer. Existing proof-difficulty and TPPS limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly announces a LeanAgent code release and supplies its repository address. Hardware, optimizer settings, sequence lengths, search budgets, repository commits, and data-splitting details were already documented in v7.

R1.justification: v8 adds references to the original DeepSeek-Prover paper and GaLore in its discussion of adapting other LLMs. It expands positioning relative to existing models and search strategies; Llemma and Hypertree Proof Search were already cited.

P1.justification: The section and appendix organization remains intact. Changes include limited abstract, introduction, and conclusion edits, expanded explanations in Appendices A.2 and A.5, author-year citations, publication-header text, and an equal-contribution note.

P2.justification: The document adopts ICLR typography, margins, headers, and widespread table and proof-panel reflow. Figure 2 is redrawn with the same examples. Tables 2 and 10 receive new accuracy-based structures, Table 2 gains a baseline column and loses the alternate-PFR row, and Tables 3–4 lose the composite-score row.

improvement.justification: The added pooled fine-tuning baseline strengthens Table 2, while narrower missing-proof claims, code-access information, and architectural caveats improve precision and reproducibility. Removing the 94% composite headline preserves the underlying metric evidence. These gains are limited by the acknowledged non-direct baseline comparison and the less specific EWC selection description; the core method and existing experimental results remain unchanged.
